# triangle

|                                 |
|---------------------------------|
| ![](reference/figures/logo.svg) |

An R package to work with the triangle distribution and logarithmic
triangle distribution

## Getting Started

Install the R package:

``` r

# Stable CRAN version
install.packages("triangle")

# OR development version from GitHub
require(devtools)
devtools::install_github("bertcarnell/triangle")
```

use the functions:

- `a` = minimum
- `b` = maximum
- `c` = mode

``` r

require(triangle)
```

### Triangle distribution

``` r

# rtriangle(n, a, b, c)
set.seed(42)
rtriangle(5, 1, 5, 2)
```

``` R
## [1] 3.988898 4.131038 2.073171 3.573596 2.926584
```

``` r

# ptriangle(x, a, b, c)
ptriangle(0:5, 0, 10, 5)
```

``` R
## [1] 0.00 0.02 0.08 0.18 0.32 0.50
```

``` r

# qtriangle(p, a, b, c)
qtriangle(seq(0, 1, by = 0.2), 1, 10, 3)
```

``` R
## [1]  1.000000  2.897367  3.851830  4.980040  6.450352 10.000000
```

``` r

# dtriangle(x, a, b, c)
dtriangle(0:4, 0, 10, 5)
```

``` R
## [1] 0.00 0.04 0.08 0.12 0.16
```

### Logarithmic triangle distribution

``` r

# rltriangle(n, a, b, c, logbase)
set.seed(2001)
rltriangle(5, 1, 100, 10)
```

``` R
## [1] 20.195183 13.001831  4.579489  4.753026  3.572658
```

``` r

# pltriangle(x, a, b, c, logbase)
pltriangle(10^(0:3), 1, 1000, 10)
```

``` R
## [1] 0.0000000 0.3333333 0.8333333 1.0000000
```

``` r

# qltriangle(p, a, b, c, logbase)
qltriangle(seq(0, 1, by = 0.2), 1, 100, 20)
```

``` R
## [1]   1.00000   5.26497  10.47630  17.76210  29.59642 100.00000
```

``` r

# dltriangle(x, a, b, c, logbase)
dltriangle(0:5, 1, 10, 5)
```

``` R
## [1] 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.8613531 1.3652124 1.7227062 2.0000000
```

### Parameter estimates

#### triangle method of moments estimates

``` r

x <- rtriangle(20, 0, 2, 1.5)
triangle_mom(x)
```

``` R
##         a         b         c 
## 0.6341961 1.9096262 1.4197678
```

#### triangle maximum likelihood estimates

``` r

x <- c(0.1, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.45, 0.6, 0.75, 0.8)
# triangle_mle(x, debug = FALSE, maxiter = 100)
triangle_mle(x)
```

``` R
## Triangle Maximum Likelihood Estimates
## 
## Call:  triangle_mle(x = x) 
## 
## Estimates:
##   Estimate Std.Err
## a -0.10366      NA
## b  0.80000      NA
## c  0.80000      NA
## 
## Convergence Code:  0
##   CONVERGENCE: REL_REDUCTION_OF_F <= FACTR*EPSMCH
```

``` r

# standard triangle (0,1) likelihood estimates
standard_triangle_mle(x)
```

``` R
## Triangle Maximum Likelihood Estimates
## 
## Call:  standard_triangle_mle(x = x) 
## 
## Estimates:
##   Estimate Std.Err
## a      0.0  0.0000
## b      1.0  0.0000
## c      0.3  0.0871
## 
## Convergence Code:  NA
##  
```

``` r

set.seed(1976)
x <- rtriangle(100, 1, 5, 3.5)
triangle_mle(x)
```

``` R
## Triangle Maximum Likelihood Estimates
## 
## Call:  triangle_mle(x = x) 
## 
## Estimates:
##   Estimate Std.Err
## a  0.69536      NA
## b  4.73677      NA
## c  4.73677      NA
## 
## Convergence Code:  0
##   CONVERGENCE: REL_REDUCTION_OF_F <= FACTR*EPSMCH
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`compare_triangle_fit()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/compare_triangle_fit.md)
  : Compare multiple triangle distributions fits
- [`rltriangle()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/ltriangle.md)
  [`dltriangle()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/ltriangle.md)
  [`pltriangle()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/ltriangle.md)
  [`qltriangle()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/ltriangle.md)
  : The Log-Triangle Distribution
- [`summary(`*`<triangle_mle>`*`)`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/mle-utils.md)
  [`print(`*`<triangle_mle>`*`)`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/mle-utils.md)
  [`coef(`*`<triangle_mle>`*`)`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/mle-utils.md)
  [`logLik(`*`<triangle_mle>`*`)`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/mle-utils.md)
  [`AIC(`*`<triangle_mle>`*`)`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/mle-utils.md)
  [`BIC(`*`<triangle_mle>`*`)`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/mle-utils.md)
  [`vcov(`*`<triangle_mle>`*`)`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/mle-utils.md)
  [`profile(`*`<triangle_mle>`*`)`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/mle-utils.md)
  [`confint(`*`<triangle_mle>`*`)`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/mle-utils.md)
  : Utility Methods for S3 class triangle_mle
- [`qqtriangle()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/qqtriangle.md)
  : Quantile-Quantile Plot for Triangle Distributed Data
- [`standard_triangle_mle()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/standard_triangle_mle.md)
  : Maximum likelihood estimate of the standard triangle distribution
  mode
- [`dtriangle()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/triangle.md)
  [`ptriangle()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/triangle.md)
  [`qtriangle()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/triangle.md)
  [`rtriangle()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/triangle.md)
  : The Triangle Distribution
- [`triangle_cdfe()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/triangle_cdfe.md)
  : Triangle parameter estimates using a non-linear fit of the empirical
  CDF
- [`triangle_mle()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/triangle_mle.md)
  : Maximum likelihood estimate of the triangle distribution parameters
- [`triangle_mom()`](https://bertcarnell.github.io/triangle/reference/triangle_mom.md)
  : Triangle distribution method of moments estimate
